title: How do we write six mixed numbers as fractions?
description: Each whole is turned into as many parts as the bottom number says, and the parts are added to the fraction already there. The board does this for six mixed numbers and checks by taking the wholes back out.
teaching_notes: One idea: whole number times bottom number, plus the top number, over the same bottom number. Watch for students who add the whole number to the top number.

source: Figure it Out (section 7.5, third block), Math Talk
video_script.why: A learner writes mixed numbers as fractions by turning each whole into parts of the bottom number.
video_script.substitution: the book's own six mixed numbers
video_script.anchor: six mixed numbers written in a list on the board
video_script.payoff_line: Each mixed number becomes a fraction with the same bottom number

final_answer.spoken: three and one fourth is thirteen fourths, seven and two thirds is twenty three thirds, nine and four ninths is eighty five ninths, three and one sixth is nineteen sixths, two and three elevenths is twenty five elevenths, and three and nine tenths is thirty nine tenths

video_script.fraction_reading: thirteen fourths, twenty three thirds, eighty five ninths, nineteen sixths, twenty five elevenths, thirty nine tenths
maths_rules: each whole = bottom number of parts, for example 1 = 4/4
the bottom number stays the same
video_script.design: Each whole bar is cut into the bottom number of parts, and all the parts are counted together with the fraction already there.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the six mixed numbers 3 1/4, 7 2/3, 9 4/9, 3 1/6, 2 3/11 and 3 9/10 in a list; the words mixed number beside a whole number and a fraction

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.def: a whole number and a fraction are written side by side and labelled mixed number
marks.one: the first three mixed numbers are written in a list
marks.two: the last three mixed numbers are written in the list
marks.ask: the question is written below the list

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, and it is about mixed numbers.
<bookmark mark='def'/>A whole number with a fraction beside it is called a mixed number.
<bookmark mark='one'/>They are three and one fourth, seven and two thirds, and nine and four ninths.
<bookmark mark='two'/>The others are three and one sixth, two and three elevenths, and three and nine tenths.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can we write each one as a fraction?

beats.on_screen: the list of mixed numbers stays; the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a whole unit bar cut into four equal parts, each labelled 1/4

marks.each: a whole unit bar is cut into as many parts as the bottom number says

narration: <bookmark mark='each'/>Each whole unit is as many parts as the bottom number says.
For example, one whole is four fourths.

beats.on_screen: Given: the six mixed numbers 3 1/4, 7 2/3, 9 4/9, 3 1/6, 2 3/11 and 3 9/10
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, six mixed numbers, each with a whole number and a fraction.

beats.on_screen: To find: each mixed number as a fraction
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each one as a fraction with one top number and one bottom number.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 3 1/4 = 3 + 1/4; 3 wholes = 3 x 4 = 12 fourths; 12 fourths + 1 fourth = 13 fourths

marks.whole: the three wholes are each cut into four fourths and counted as twelve fourths
marks.add: the one fourth already there is added to the twelve fourths

narration: <bookmark mark='whole'/>Step one, we use the same way as the example in your book. Each whole is four fourths, so three wholes are twelve fourths.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Add the one fourth that is already there. Twelve fourths and one fourth are thirteen fourths.

marks.thirds: seven wholes are turned into twenty one thirds and two thirds are added
marks.ninths: nine wholes are turned into eighty one ninths and four ninths are added

narration: <bookmark mark='thirds'/>Step two, seven times three is twenty one, and adding two gives twenty three thirds.
<bookmark mark='ninths'/>Nine times nine is eighty one, and adding four gives eighty five ninths.

marks.sixths: three wholes are turned into eighteen sixths and one sixth is added
marks.elevenths: two wholes are turned into twenty two elevenths and three elevenths are added
marks.tenths: three wholes are turned into thirty tenths and nine tenths are added

narration: <bookmark mark='sixths'/>Step three, three times six is eighteen, and adding one gives nineteen sixths.
<bookmark mark='elevenths'/>Two times eleven is twenty two, and adding three gives twenty five elevenths.
<bookmark mark='tenths'/>Three times ten is thirty, and adding nine gives thirty nine tenths.

beats.on_screen: Check: 13 fourths = 12 fourths + 1 fourth = 3 wholes + 1/4; 23 thirds = 21 thirds + 2 thirds; 85 ninths = 81 ninths + 4 ninths

marks.first: thirteen fourths is split into twelve fourths, which make three wholes, and one fourth
marks.others: twenty three thirds and eighty five ninths are split into wholes and a leftover in the same way

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>To check, take the wholes back out of each fraction. Thirteen fourths is twelve fourths and one fourth, which is three and one fourth.
<bookmark mark='others'/>Twenty three thirds has seven wholes and two thirds left. Eighty five ninths has nine wholes and four ninths left.

marks.first: the first three answers are read
marks.last: the last three answers are read

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Each mixed number becomes a fraction with the same bottom number.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Three and one fourth is thirteen fourths. Seven and two thirds is twenty three thirds. Nine and four ninths is eighty five ninths.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Three and one sixth is nineteen sixths. Two and three elevenths is twenty five elevenths. Three and nine tenths is thirty nine tenths.
